SALAH recording recognition beta, 2026-10-18, revision 369

221 indexed recordings by 46 library voices. Most newly added voices have short surahs 1, 112, 113 and 114; partial catalogues use available short surahs. This is recording identification, not arbitrary live voice identification. The Quran screen lists the exact indexed surahs. Yasser verse/continuous variants represent one voice.

Sources, SHA-256 fingerprints and available timing boundaries are in catalog-v2.json. The original acoustic landmark implementation runs on the device. Reference MP3s are not distributed, only non-reconstructive landmarks and timing data. Recordings from verse libraries are assembled from the exact published ayah files; boundaries come from decoded sample counts. Full-surah ayah labels require a complete timing table for that recording and duration validation. If unavailable, the result explicitly shows only surah and reciter. No estimated ayah numbers.

Build scripts: build-quran-recognition.mjs (original 69 references), expand-quran-recognition.mjs (152 additional references). Seven attempted references were rejected due to source/decode failure; other recordings still cover those voices. Source MP3 acquisition is documented in docs/recognition-expansion-369.md.

Calibration: 303/304 independently cropped clean 6/8-second reference excerpts matched correctly; one no-match and zero incorrect identities in that fixture. CI additionally checks the original clean/echo fixtures, every new voice and silence/tones. These figures are not real-device microphone accuracy claims.

Queries now keep anchors from every time frame instead of skipping alternating frames, eliminating a major dependence on the sample start phase. Reference indexes stay sparse to keep downloads small. Default recording is 8 seconds; the base is downloaded during microphone permission/recording. Audio is never uploaded.
